one_liner: Senior Executive Service job running the federal panel that resolves bargaining deadlocks between federal agencies and unions, managing staff, cases, budget and stakeholder relations.
fit_summary: This SES role requires executive leadership plus deep labor-management dispute-resolution expertise (mediation, arbitration, adjudication). Daniel's resume shows neither, so skip it.
eligibility: Open to the public, including applicants with no prior federal service; hiring paths include public and SES, and no clearance is required.

You must show both Technical Qualifications in your resume: TQ 1, dispute-resolution techniques for labor or employment disputes, and TQ 2, expertise in labor-management relations and/or employment matters.
You must show all five Executive Core Qualifications in the resume itself; separate narratives are not accepted, and OPM's QRB must certify you before appointment.
The resume is strictly limited to 2 pages, 10pt Arial or Times New Roman, with 1-inch margins, or you are immediately ineligible.
If selected, you would serve a one-year SES probationary period.
strategy: Skip this one: it requires SES-level executive leadership plus labor-management dispute-resolution expertise, and his resume shows neither.
Put the time into emergency management, public health preparedness, or program analyst roles where his resume fits.
resume_bullets: Worked with FEMA, state agencies, local governments and a large travel company across seven years at IEM (2019–2026).
Led a five-person intake center for ReBuild NC after Hurricane Matthew (2019).
interview_questions: Describe a labor or employment dispute you helped resolve, including the method you used and the outcome.
How would you manage the Panel's case intake and decide which resolution procedure fits a given impasse?
Tell us about a time you cut waste or improved efficiency in an organization you led.
How have you held staff accountable while leading them through change?
watch_outs: The TQs require labor-relations and dispute-resolution expertise that is not in your known background, so you will likely be screened out without it.
SES-level executive experience is expected, and QRB certification is a demanding extra hurdle.
Any formatting violation on the 2-page resume results in automatic disqualification.
The role is based in Washington, DC and is telework-eligible but not remote, so expect a commute from Manassas.
